questions.stem: What does ESP stand for in data processing?
options: Event-Stream Processing
Enterprise Storage Platform
Extract, Store and Publish
External Service Provider
Encrypted Stream Protocol
questions.explanation: ESP is Event-Stream Processing, a term used alongside CDC and Real-Time processing.

questions.stem: How is Event-Stream Processing related to Real-Time processing?
options: ESP is the batch alternative to Real-Time
ESP replaces Real-Time in modern systems
ESP only applies to CCTV streams
ESP is exactly what Real-Time is all about
ESP is a slower form of CDC
questions.explanation: ESP is exactly what Real-Time is all about: the moment an activity happens in the source, the latest action is pushed to the next stage.

questions.stem: In what situation is Event-Stream Processing heavily used?
options: When data is loaded once a month
When a reaction is planned in Real-Time
When data must be archived for compliance
When a data model needs normalising
When historical trends are analysed years later
questions.explanation: Event-Stream Processing is heavily used if a reaction is planned in Real-Time.

questions.stem: Which of the following can be the next stage that receives an event in Event-Stream Processing?
options: A printed report
A tape backup
A monthly spreadsheet
An email archive
A Data Lake, a Data Warehouse, or an intermediate in-memory solution preparing a response for the customer's mobile
questions.explanation: The next stage can be a Data Lake or Data Warehouse, or an intermediate in-memory solution that prepares a response to send directly back to the customer's mobile.

questions.stem: In the shopping mall example of Event-Stream Processing, what arrives on the customer's mobile along with the OTP code when they pay by card?
options: A request to confirm their address
A copy of the receipt
A message telling them about a sale or promotion in the mall to look at before paying
A password reset link
A survey about the shop
questions.explanation: The moment the card is used, along with the OTP another message tells the customer there is a sale or promotion in the mall, which is Real-Time Event-Stream Processing.

questions.stem: In the ATM example of Event-Stream Processing, what does the application discover?
options: That the account balance is too low
That the same card was used in another ATM 1000 km away in the last 10 minutes
That the PIN was entered incorrectly
That the card has expired
That the ATM is out of cash
questions.explanation: With Event-Stream Processing the application finds the same card was used 1000 km away within 10 minutes, which no one could travel.

questions.stem: In the ATM example of Event-Stream Processing, what action does the application take once it detects the impossible travel?
options: It sends a promotional message
It dispenses the cash anyway
It emails the bank manager the next day
It asks the customer to re-enter the PIN
It immediately locks the door of the room where the ATM is stationed
questions.explanation: Knowing no one can travel 1000 km in 10 minutes, the application immediately locks the door where the ATM is stationed.

questions.stem: Which source systems are named as places where an activity can trigger Event-Stream Processing?
options: An online portal, social media or a mobile
A tape library or an archive
A printed ledger
A monthly report
A data dictionary
questions.explanation: The source system or application can be an online portal, social media, a mobile and so on; the moment any activity takes place, the latest action is pushed to the next stage.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about Event-Stream Processing is NOT correct?
options: It is used together with CDC and Real-Time processing
It pushes the latest action the moment an activity happens
It processes events in overnight batches
It can feed a Data Lake or Data Warehouse
It can trigger an immediate response to a customer
questions.explanation: Event-Stream Processing is about pushing each action the moment it happens, not about overnight batches.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of an intermediate in-memory solution in Event-Stream Processing?
options: To archive events for seven years
To normalise the data model
To compress the events before storage
To prepare a response to send directly back to the customer's mobile
To mask personal data
questions.explanation: The next stage can be an intermediate in-memory solution used to prepare a response that is sent directly back to the customer's mobile.
